text.p: Severe flooding is ongoing in the US North Plains across many river systems. The next few days should feature cooler than normal temperatures and no widespread heavy, precipitation. Cool temperatures keep snowmelt slow, preventing even worse flooding.

Typhoon Isa, with 85 mph winds, is near 10n/150e, moving west at 15 mph. Isa will continue to strengthen while tracking westward and then turning more to the north thereafter. Isa will threaten the Northern Mariana Islands, including Guam by 48 hours. Top winds could be near 130 mph by that time. Destructive winds, heavy rains, and a powerful, damaging storm surge are possible at that time.
There are no further emergency statements at this time.
